blocks.section: ## 0. Responsibility and evidence boundary
blocks.text: This study owns a shared question: how Pandemonium's members make company with Ibuki when affection, office, dependence, pleasure and coercion pull in different directions. Its existing ensemble home contains two substantial named responsibilities, Makoto→Ibuki and Iroha→Ibuki. They are retained as distinct directions within this one parent, with Ibuki's answers central to each. They are not two additional denominator packages. The separate institutional question about Pandemonium's roles, resources and selective care, the Kayoko–Ako boundary question, and the five individual character monographs remain separate responsibilities. An accepted character portrait cannot stand in for this account of encounters, changed participation and competing recipients.

blocks.section: ## 1. Core thesis: company survives through differentiated answers
blocks.text: Pandemonium's company with Ibuki is strongest where a member stops treating her affection as a guaranteed return. Makoto can love her company while wanting her admiration, treating her comfort selectively, or borrowing her innocence to make a leadership scene appealing. Iroha can recognize her preferences and offer protection while wanting quiet, leaving the organization, hiding information, or using her hurt to increase a punishment. Ibuki can enjoy both members, be frightened, make mistakes, want to help and refuse a proposed return. These directions do not add up to one benevolent family essence or one covertly manipulative machine. Their repeated encounters put the recipients' answers between a giver's account of care and the action that follows. ([Private account][PS01], Pandemonium lines 502–512; [pudding trilogy][PS35], §14; [MAIN return visit][PS14].)

blocks.section: ## 1. Core thesis: company survives through differentiated answers
blocks.text: A promise about pudding makes that distinction unusually clear. In MINI15030, Makoto's apology becomes acceptable when Ibuki asks her not to take **anyone's** pudding, not simply to remember that Ibuki's dessert is special. The finger promise and forgiveness are real represented ends. The ten replacement puddings remain Makoto's account, and no general account of future compliance follows. What changes in the encounter is the terms under which Ibuki agrees to resume company: her grievance is heard, her own answer is sought, and the wrong's scope widens beyond a favored child. That is a relational achievement with an unfinished afterlife, not an institutional acquittal. ([MINI32][PS35], §14, MINI15030:u0088–0114.)

blocks.section: ## 1. Core thesis: company survives through differentiated answers
blocks.text: Iroha's offered exit establishes a different achievement. In MAIN S2V002C2E011, she offers Ibuki hair combing, reading and company away from the changed Makoto. Ibuki likes the offer and nevertheless chooses to remain because Makoto is lonely. Iroha checks that this is what she wants and accepts the answer. Respect is visible in the option and in accepting refusal of that option. It would be an error to count only removal from Makoto as protective care, just as it would be an error to turn Ibuki's choice into proof that the environment is safe or that she understands every political danger. The scene gives an answer to an offered course of action; its worth is not cancelled by the missing safety certificate. ([MAIN return visit][PS14], u0041–0110.)

blocks.section: ## 1. Core thesis: company survives through differentiated answers
blocks.text: The ensemble's ordinary ends make those answers intelligible. Ibuki wants to play, taste things, make a collage, see a parade, help with work and spend time with people she likes. Iroha wants rest and chosen reading, not only the opportunity to serve. Makoto wants admired company and sometimes obtains it through genuine practical adjustment. Satsuki wants relief, food and reassuring contact; Chiaki wants scenes worth seeing and recording. These are ends whose partial achievement and frustration matter before they become examples of political virtue or crisis resilience. A child wanting more time with PS68 is not valuable only because the request chastens a leader. A quiet outing is not discarded because no government changes. ([Private account][PS01], lines 502–510; [MINI32][PS35], §§12,14; [summer account][PS04], 001–015.)

blocks.section: ## 1. Core thesis: company survives through differentiated answers
blocks.text: The synthesis is consequently about the distribution of choice within shared participation. Makoto and Iroha differ in what they notice, offer, withhold and ask back. Ibuki's agency is neither adult sovereignty nor passive moral symbolism. The social structure permits real kindness and real asymmetry together. It changes locally when members act on an answer that complicates their own preferred story: a refused return, a refusal to issue a stay order, a child who already knows about a quarrel, or a member who does not want another photograph. No uniform affection score can replace these encounters. ([MINI32][PS35], §14; [summer account][PS04], 004–005,012–014.)

blocks.section: ## 2. Longitudinal arc: locally ordered changes, independent recurring contexts
blocks.text: Three internally ordered sequences provide the strongest changes. The MINI150 trilogy moves from a repeated pudding offense and Ibuki's departure, through discovery and chosen play with PS68, to the apology, wider promise and farewell. MAIN S2V002 moves from the abnormal drive toward unanimity, through Iroha's departure and the private return visit, to coordinated resistance, local recovery, Makoto's apology and public promises. EVENT860 moves through the narrated drifting days, disagreements, pirate-ship encounter, escape, medical aftermath and wanted continuing company. Each sequence gives development. Their coexistence is not a warrant to arrange every private variant and event into one maturation ladder. ([MINI32][PS35], §14; [MAIN checkpoints][PS06], [PS08]; [summer account][PS04], source-form and item accounts.)

blocks.section: ## 2. Longitudinal arc: locally ordered changes, independent recurring contexts
blocks.text: Within the pudding sequence, departure is followed by encounter rather than immediate return. Ibuki is lost and feels sorry for harsh words while retaining a valid grievance about the theft. Aru offers an escort; Ibuki refuses it. When the searchers find her, she rejects a kidnapping interpretation and says she left voluntarily. Being no longer angry does not mean she is ready to stop playing. Her later forgiveness is situated after this interval of wanted company and her own condition on Makoto. Treating the middle as mere logistical delay would remove the child's independent time and make return a foregone senior-member objective. ([MINI32][PS35], MINI15010:u0064–0097; MINI15020:u0025–0077; MINI15030:u0088–0114.)

blocks.section: ## 2. Longitudinal arc: locally ordered changes, independent recurring contexts
blocks.text: MAIN has a more severe local separation. Makoto's demand for unity depicts dissent as a defective screw; Iroha verbally leaves, and Makoto accepts that choice while later practical burdens show its cost. Chiaki notices the emptied social atmosphere and a hiatus in her newspaper. Ibuki is low and alone with a busy Makoto. Iroha's return visit expressly does not mean she has rejoined. Later she coordinates work across former opponents, appeals to Makoto under an unresolved counterbroadcast mechanism, and receives an actual apology. The movement is not private affection automatically transferring into a public cure. It involves distinct choices, other contributors and explicitly incomplete causal knowledge. ([MAIN departure][PS10]; [Chiaki interview][PS11]; [return visit][PS14]; [coalition][PS13], [PS18]; [recovery][PS19].)

blocks.text: The public aftermath preserves an important adverse remainder. Makoto withdraws the battle plan and promises property return, while students report ammunition not yet restored, unwanted contribution points and anxiety at another assembly. The local recovery and speech are achieved; restitution, recurrence prevention and technical explanation remain unfinished. Both kinds of end must survive the ensemble account. blocks.section: ## 2. Longitudinal arc: locally ordered changes, independent recurring contexts
blocks.text: EVENT860 supplies a sequence of company that includes failures of recognition. Makoto's costly rental decision is real, and she immediately denies Ibuki's self-blame. Iroha spares the child worry, but Ibuki later reveals she already knows about their drifting and quarrel. Iroha apologizes for her own volume without retracting her complaint, and later refuses work until Makoto apologizes; Satsuki doubts that a forced formal apology would solve the problem. Makoto then refuses to order her to remain, articulating free choice even amid a badly managed situation. They later contribute differently to survival, quarrel and rescue, and return to wanted company. This arc cannot be rewritten as unbroken harmony or reduced to incompetent older members corrected by a pure child. ([Summer account][PS04], 002–005,007–014.)

blocks.section: ## 2. Longitudinal arc: locally ordered changes, independent recurring contexts
blocks.text: The Eden and Final appearances complicate, rather than complete, this development. In Eden, Iroha corrects Makoto's imagined Schale alliance, Makoto later self-claims a destructive Arius bargain, Ibuki sees dangerous boxes and an explosion follows. Rescue is later reported, and Iroha urges Makoto to rest in the epilogue. Neither sequence authorizes attaching a single recurring pudding incident to all the others. The ensemble can repeat an interpretive pressure—favored company enabling and redirecting action—without asserting a shared global date or identical offense. blocks.text: The private normal account restores kinds of attention that the public office plot cannot supply by itself. blocks.section: ## 3. Public and private selves: care does not settle its recipients' claims
blocks.text: Ibuki's private repertoire is equally resistant to summary as cuteness. Failed park, carousel and parade plans differ from actually fulfilled local games and pleasant time. She gets help down after finding shade; that is not independent descent. She actually eats corn and feels full in one context, while an offered rice ball elsewhere has no printed consumption. Her half-empty collage comes from too few collected materials rather than a fabricated lack of paper. Wanted careers conclude with partial understanding and thanks, not an enacted arrest, profession or meal. These small distinctions keep her initiative, frustration and appetite distinct from the older members' stories about what she needs. ([Private account][PS01], line 506.)

blocks.section: ## 3. Public and private selves: care does not settle its recipients' claims
blocks.text: Satsuki's relief and appetite and Chiaki's curiosity broaden the ensemble beyond two rival carers. Satsuki's food, escort, hand-held reassurance and night paperwork coexist with failed methods, adults refusing, fatigue and exploiting vulnerability. Chiaki's shared newspaper, tasting, visits and excited return coexist with an unsuccessful tenth macaron, unusable images and lost notes. Encouragement does not recover her notebook or publish an article. In photographs and private contact, permission is particular: an invitation to look does not erase a later request not to look or to stay still, and departure or a withdrawn message does not become ongoing consent. Their own wants and limits are part of the company Ibuki joins. ([Private account][PS01], lines 508–510.)

blocks.section: ## 4. School and club role: participation exceeds office, while labor still has costs
blocks.text: The ensemble lives within an office that distributes work unequally. Iroha's departure makes Makoto perform practical tasks herself; Chiaki sees a potential scoop in this change. The old newspaper's hiatus and the members' absence make the room less lively. These are social and administrative effects of a person's absence, not evidence that the organization has legally dissolved. The member is wanted partly for what she does and partly for the company she makes. A reading that names only labor extraction misses the latter; a reading that names only family affection conceals the former. ([MAIN Chiaki account][PS11], u0001–0014.)

blocks.section: ## 6. Named duty P3-REL-MAKOTO-IBUKI: selective affection meets a wider promise
blocks.text: Makoto→Ibuki is a direction of attention whose giver often wants an answer back: admiration, reassurance, a place beside the child, or restored favor. Ibuki→Makoto includes wanted play, worry for her loneliness, forgiveness and requests for other people's benefit. The two are not identical motivations exchanged symmetrically. Makoto holds office and can mobilize resources; Ibuki's choices are local and situated among older members. The meaningful reciprocity is therefore not equal power but a visible capacity to answer, refuse and alter the terms of closeness. Reading only Makoto's declared affection would miss the very feedback through which this relationship becomes intelligible. ([MINI32][PS35],§§2,14; [MAIN return visit][PS14]; [Final rescue][PS33].)
